steps.title: Turn the playbook into rules: position, fallback, walk-away
steps.what: The firm's written playbook became 8 rules, each with a position, a fallback, a walk-away and a machine-readable check.
steps.output:
Confidentiality term
  position:  Confidentiality obligations last no more than 3 years after disclosure.
  fallback:  3 years, with trade secrets protected for as long as they remain trade secrets.
  walk-away: Perpetual obligations for all information, or a term longer than 7 years.
Limitation of liability
  position:  Total liability capped at the fees paid in the 12 months before the claim.
  fallback:  Cap at fees paid in the prior 24 months, with carve-outs only for confidentiality breach and indemnity.
  walk-away: Uncapped or unlimited liability for our client.
Indemnification
  position:  Mutual indemnities, each limited to third-party claims.
  fallback:  Mutual indemnities for third-party IP and confidentiality claims, subject to the liability cap.
  walk-away: One-sided indemnity from our client that is not subject to any cap.
Governing law
  position:  Delaware or New York law.
  fallback:  Any US state law, with venue in that state's courts.
  walk-away: Non-US governing law.
... and 4 more rules in playbook.json

steps.title: Package rules, clause library and scripts as one Skill
steps.what: One folder holds the instructions, rules, approved fallback wording and the redline script; frontmatter has name and description, and 8/8 rules have library wording.
steps.code:
skill/contract-review/
  SKILL.md            # name + description frontmatter, review steps
  playbook.json       # rules
  clause_library.json # approved fallbacks
  scripts/redline.py  # .docx redline + memo

steps.title: Mark each clause OK / negotiate / escalate with a reason
steps.what: Claude, loaded with the Skill, reviewed 10 contracts (58 clauses): 20 OK, 18 negotiate, 20 escalate.
steps.code:
system = SKILL.md + playbook.json + clause_library.json
reviews = batch_structured(system=system, items=contracts,

steps.title: Output a redlined .docx and a one-page issues memo
steps.what: Wrote 10 redlines and 10 memos; CT-05's redline has 1 struck clause(s) with library fallbacks inserted and a Word comment on every flagged clause.
steps.code:
old = p.add_run(clause_text); old.font.strike = True
new = p.add_run(LIBRARY[clause_type]); new.font.underline = True
doc.add_comment([old, new], text=f"Negotiate: {reason}")
write_memo(contract, review, RULES, LIBRARY, memo_path)

steps.title: Test on 10 past contracts against what partners changed
steps.what: Compared 58 clause calls with the partner's final decisions: 88% agreement, 95% of partner escalations caught.

steps.title: Compare with how associates reviewed the same contracts
steps.what: Three associates' past calls on the same clauses are the baseline for consistency and partner edits.
steps.code:
consistency_before = share of clauses where all 3 associates agreed
consistency_after = share of clauses with the same call on a second run
partner_edits = clauses per contract where the call differs from the partner

story.situation: A commercial team reviews dozens of NDAs and MSAs a month. Associates redline the same issues by hand, and each applies the playbook a little differently, so partners keep re-editing.
story.constraints: Client documents are confidential and stay inside the firm's Claude workspace (a Project per client). Fallback wording must come from the approved clause library, never be drafted on the fly. Walk-away terms always go to a partner.
story.replay: Reuse: playbook-as-Skill fits any team that applies written rules to documents (procurement terms, lease abstracts, policy checks). Next time: have partners label 20 contracts before writing the rules, and track why partners override the playbook so the rules improve.
story.problem_cost: About 90 minutes of associate time per contract, plus partner time re-editing inconsistent redlines.

metrics.review_time_per_contract: 89 min -> 21 min (estimate: 10 min + 3 min per flagged clause)
metrics.consistency: 50% of clauses where 3 associates agree -> 100% same call on rerun
